planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil; this hybrid tolerates heavier shade than most Bergenia cultivars.

directions: Beethoven is part of a small group of English hybrid Bergenia named for composers, raised from a cross involving Bergenia stracheyi and B. crassifolia. Clusters of pinkish-white flowers open in early spring above broad, leathery, rounded leaves that deepen to reddish tones once cold weather sets in. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring, replanting divisions immediately into moist, humus-rich soil. It tolerates both heavier shade and drier soil than many lungwort relatives, making it a reliable evergreen edging plant.

common_name: Bach Bergenia (Red-Calyxed Pale Pink Composer Series Pigsqueak)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; winter foliage color is strongest in a site with some direct sun.

directions: Bach belongs to the same English composer-named Bergenia breeding line as 'Beethoven' and 'Brahms'. Densely packed heads of pale pink flowers that mature to near white appear in mid-spring, dramatically set off by red calyxes and flower stems. The neat, glossy foliage flushes bronze-red through winter before greening up again in spring. Divide crowded clumps every few years and keep soil consistently moist but well drained to avoid root rot.

common_name: Brahms Bergenia (White-Flowered Light-Shade Composer Series Pigsqueak)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in ordinary, moisture-retentive garden soil; tolerates light shade to full shade better than many Bergenia selections.

directions: Brahms is another of the composer-named Bergenia hybrids, valued for white spring flowers held above handsome, leathery foliage and for performing well in deeper shade than most pigsqueak selections. Divide established clumps in early spring, replanting at the same depth into humus-rich soil. Keep soil evenly moist during the first growing season; once established it is drought-tolerant and needs little care beyond removing tatty winter leaves.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, humus-rich soil; compact habit suits border fronts and containers.

directions: Britten, the last of the composer-named Bergenia introductions, holds an RHS Award of Garden Merit for its free-flowering habit. Abundant spring flowers open white and age to soft pink above small, shiny green leaves edged in bronze that deepen to red through winter. Its compact, well-behaved clumps make it a good choice for border fronts and large containers. Divide every three to four years in spring to maintain vigor.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; part of the long-running Bressingham Gardens breeding series.

directions: Bressingham Bountiful is a compact, evergreen selection from the Bressingham Gardens breeding program, the same line that produced 'Bressingham Ruby' and 'Bressingham White'. Upright stems carry dark rose-pink flower clusters in mid-spring above erect, mid-green leaves that pick up red edging as temperatures drop in fall and winter. Divide congested clumps every few years in spring and keep soil evenly moist through the first season to establish a strong root system.

common_name: Mount Nachi Saxifraga (Compact White-Flowered Fortune's Saxifrage)

planting.note: Plant divisions or potted starts in spring in humus-rich, reliably moist soil in shade to part shade; mulch over winter in colder zones.

directions: Mount Nachi was collected in the wild in Japan and is prized among Saxifraga fortunei forms for its dense, compact habit and airy sprays of small white flowers held well above the rounded, scalloped foliage in autumn. Grow in consistently moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in shade to part shade, sheltered from drying wind. Divide clumps in spring every few years to maintain vigor, and apply a winter mulch anywhere temperatures regularly drop below 0°F.

common_name: Tory MP Corydalis (Scented Blue Hybrid Fumewort)

planting.note: Plant divisions or potted starts in spring in cool, humus-rich, well-drained soil; mulch roots in summer to keep them cool and slightly moist.

directions: Tory MP is a hybrid between the two blue-flowered Chinese species Corydalis flexuosa and C. elata, introduced by a UK specialty nursery. It produces bright, sweetly scented blue flowers on reddish stems over a long season from late spring onward, taller and more vigorous than many flexuosa selections. Grow in humus-rich, evenly moist, well-drained soil in part shade, and divide congested clumps in early spring. Plants can go summer-dormant in hot climates; withhold heavy watering once foliage dies back.

common_name: Bronze Form Rodgersia (Bellevue Botanical Garden Chocolate-New-Growth Rodgersia)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring along a stream bank, pond margin, or any consistently moist, humus-rich shaded site; roots should never dry out.

directions: Bronze Form was selected at Washington's Bellevue Botanical Garden for its richly colored new growth, which emerges red-tinged chocolate-bronze before settling to dark green through midsummer, then flushing copper and maroon again in autumn. Large, deeply veined, horse-chestnut-like leaves top sturdy stems bearing creamy-white to pale pink plumes in early summer. Grow in reliably moist, humus-rich soil along a stream bank or pond margin, since the foliage scorches quickly if the roots dry out. Divide crowded clumps in early spring.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall in humus-rich, well-drained woodland soil; cut back old foliage in late winter before new flower spikes emerge.

directions: Spring Wedding is a grandiflorum selection grown for its new foliage, which emerges with narrow red margins around green centers before settling to plain green in summer. Pale lavender, long-spurred flowers hover above the leaves on wiry stems in mid-spring. Shear old foliage to the ground in late winter so the flowers are not hidden, and grow in humus-rich, well-drained soil in shade to light woodland dapple. Divide congested clumps after flowering every three to four years.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall in humus-rich, well-drained woodland soil; coldest winter weather brings out the darkest foliage color.

directions: Black Sea is grown chiefly for its foliage display: leaves stay green through spring and summer but turn a striking near-black as cold weather arrives, holding that color through much of winter in milder climates. Small spring flowers are a secondary feature next to the dramatic winter leaf color. Grow in humus-rich, well-drained soil in shade, mulching with leaf litter to mimic its native woodland floor. Divide clumps after flowering every few years to maintain a dense groundcover effect.

common_name: Pretty in Pink Pulmonaria (Consistently Pink-Flowered Lungwort)

planting.note: Plant divisions in early spring or fall in humus-rich, consistently moist soil in part shade to full shade.

directions: Pretty in Pink is a Walters Gardens introduction bred to hold its bright rose-pink flower color rather than shifting toward blue or purple as the blooms age, a trait that sets it apart from most Pulmonaria cultivars. Large flower clusters open in early spring above dark green leaves lightly speckled with silver. Grow in evenly moist, humus-rich soil in part to full shade, and divide congested clumps in early spring or immediately after flowering. Shear foliage back hard after bloom if powdery mildew appears in a hot, dry summer.

common_name: Diamonds and Pearls Astilbe (Drought-Tolerant Silvery-White Chinensis Astilbe)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in humus-rich soil; chinensis-type astilbes tolerate drier soil than Japonica or Arendsii types once established.

directions: Diamonds and Pearls forms a tidy, upright, free-flowering clump topped in early summer with densely packed, diamond-shaped plumes of tiny pure white flowers. Like other Astilbe chinensis selections it handles drier soil better than most astilbes, though flowering and foliage quality are best with consistent moisture. Grow in humus-rich soil in part shade, and divide crowded clumps every three to four years in early spring to maintain vigorous bloom.

common_name: Rhythm and Blues Astilbe (Raspberry-Pink Music Series False Spirea)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in consistently moist, humus-rich soil; part of the compact, heavy-flowering Music series bred in the Netherlands.

directions: Rhythm and Blues belongs to the Music series, a group of Dutch-bred compact astilbes selected for dense, floriferous plumes and attractive foliage. Full, fuzzy, raspberry-pink plumes form a diamond-shaped bloom in early to midsummer over a shorter, sturdier plant than older Arendsii cultivars. Keep soil consistently moist, since astilbe foliage scorches quickly in dry conditions, and divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring.
